human_tolerance.notes: Authored judgement from Wikipedia: roe deer keep to forest refuge by day and use open habitat mainly at night and crepuscular times; not an urban exploiter.

phases.name: mating
phases.note: Rut (breeding season) in July and August per Wikipedia; mating in early autumn is also mentioned there.

vocalizations.description: Short dog-like bark given when alarmed, with a flash of the white rump patch.
High-pitched 'pheep' whine from does attracting bucks during the rut in July and August.

taxonomy.note: Accepted name Capreolus capreolus (Linnaeus, 1758), species rank; GBIF checked 2026-11-01.

external.note: GBIF usageKey 5220126; iNaturalist taxon 42184 and NCBI 9858 via Wikidata P3151 and P685.

range.note: Partial country-level range from Wikipedia's distribution section, which describes mainland Britain, noting the historical 1884 German introduction in Thetford alongside separate British range expansions. GB represents species-level native range, while the country-level schema cannot distinguish native Scottish populations from historical introductions and subsequent spread in parts of England. Israel remains listed as introduced from the documented 1991 introduction. This is not a complete distribution.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Authored. No open source with roe deer gait or speed was found on 2026-11-01 (one standard web search); Walk, Trot and Gallop are set to match the shared ground-forager program's flee gait. Reviewer should confirm.

traits.thermoregulation.note: Mammal class-level trait; Wikipedia describes the species as well adapted to cold environments.

traits.nest_type.note: Does not build a nest; beds in leaf litter (Wikipedia Behaviour).

traits.mass_kg.note: EltonTraits BodyMass 22500 g (Smith et al. 2003 via Ref_117); Wikipedia average weight 20-25 kg.

traits.length_m.note: Midpoint of Wikipedia body length 95-135 cm.

traits.shoulder_height_m.note: Midpoint of Wikipedia shoulder height 63-67 cm.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Wikipedia: 'A normal life span in the wild is seven to eight years, or ten years.' Set to 8, the upper end of the first stated range. Sources disagree: ADW (NC, 'approximately ten years'; not used) and AnAge via ADW ('Average lifespan, wild 15.0 years'; licence not verified, not used). Not a maximum or captive value.

traits.diet.note: EltonTraits Diet-PlantO 100 (plant material only; Diet-Source Ref_1). Wikipedia: 'mainly grass, leaves, berries, and young shoots'. The 50/50 browse/graze split is authored: no source gives proportions.

traits.social.note: Territorial; does and bucks defend territories, same-sex neighbours excluded (Wikipedia). Solitary with occasional family groups (ADW, not used). Group size 1-3 is authored.

traits.activity_pattern.note: EltonTraits flags nocturnal, crepuscular and diurnal all at 1. Wikipedia: refuge in forest by day, open habitat at night and crepuscular times. Crepuscular chosen.

traits.defense.note: Flees and barks when alarmed (Wikipedia Behaviour).

habitat.note: Authored placement: forest refuge, open habitat at night (Wikipedia Behaviour); bed in leaf litter; graze and browse from Wikipedia Diet.

seasonal.note: Rut in July and August (Wikipedia Behaviour: does 'pheep' during the rut in July and August).

vocalizations.note: Descriptions from Wikipedia Behaviour. cooldown_s values (10 and 30) are authored judgement.

behavior.note: Species-local fsm-capreolus-forager-v1 has reachable browse and graze states, each requiring its matching resource tag. Both use walking; threat responses use gallop. Any non-flee state yields to shrub_thicket rest when solar elevation is 10 to 90 degrees; rest exits when energy need is below 0.2 and the sun leaves that window. Wikipedia's Habitat section says roe deer retreat to dense woodland or bramble scrub to rest. Outside the daytime window the program permits activity at any time, consistent with crepuscular rather than strictly nocturnal activity.

look.note: Colours from Wikipedia ('reddish and grey-brown'; heart- or kidney-shaped white rump patch). Proportions and parts are authored judgement, not measured.
